dicas.texto: Você sabe que 9/9 é igual a 1 inteiro. Se você tem 10/9, você tem um inteiro completo e mais quanto?
Tente clicar no botão 'Convert'. Isso vai te ajudar a separar o inteiro da parte fracionária, facilitando a marcação na reta.
Ao converter 10/9, você terá 1 inteiro e mais 1/9. O ponto deve ficar um pouco depois do número 1 na reta.
O número 1 na reta numérica corresponde a 9/9. Como você precisa de 10/9, conte apenas uma marcação (1/9) à direita do número 1.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 9 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

campo: numerador da parte fracionária do número misto ("-" quando não há)

reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)
grupo com m1/m2/m3, exibido depois de Convert
botão "Convert": abre as caixas do número misto (m1, m2, m3) para reescrever a fração
campo numérico da caixa de cima da fração (numerador)
campo numérico: parte inteira do número misto

dicas.texto: Which part of a fraction tells how many parts are being counted?
Look at the number positioned above the fraction bar in the problem.
The numerator is the first number written in the fraction.
Type the top number of the fraction into the upper box.
Which part of a fraction tells how many equal parts make one whole?
Look at the number positioned below the fraction bar in the problem.
The denominator is the second number written in the fraction.
Type the bottom number of the fraction into the lower box.
Compare the numerator with the denominator to decide whether the fraction is greater than one.
A fraction is greater than one when its numerator is larger than its denominator.
The numerator is larger than the denominator in this problem, so conversion is needed.
Use the button labeled Convert to open the mixed-number entry fields.
A mixed number shows the whole groups first and the leftover fractional part second.
Divide the numerator by the denominator; use the quotient as the whole number and the remainder as the new numerator.
The denominator stays the same in the fractional part, while the remainder goes above it.
Fill the whole-number field with the quotient, the fractional numerator field with the remainder, and the fractional denominator field with the original denominator.
First locate one whole, then determine whether the fraction lies just before or just after that whole.
Use the denominator to count equal intervals in each unit and the numerator to count those intervals from zero.
Nine equal intervals reach 1, so the next interval after 1 is the target location.
Starting at 1, move forward one of the ninth-sized intervals and place the point there.
Before submitting, check that the fraction and its location on the number line represent the same value.
Review the numerator, denominator, mixed number, and marked point in order.
The point should be one ninth past 1, and the mixed-number fields should show one whole with one ninth remaining.
When every field and the number-line point are correct, click the button labeled Done.

exercicio.statement:
Sean's baseball team played against Barry's team. The two teams were tied after nine innings, so the game went into extra innings. Sean's team won the game in the tenth inning. Usually a game only lasts nine innings, but since they played a tenth, Sean and Barry's game lasted 10/9 as long as a normal game. Show 10/9 on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?
